newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end slightly up in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end slightly up in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Thursday in mixed trading with small- and medium-capitalization shares posting the biggest gains, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.24 percent, or 0.50 points, to 206.89 on all-share turnover of 90 million shekels against 105 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.02 percent to 214.95.
"Trading was mixed today and we saw some profit taking. The attack (on Jewish settlers) had no impact on trading today," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.
On Wednesday a Jewish settler and her 12-year-old son were killed by Palestinians in the West Bank.

"Activity is moving from the blue chips to small- and medium-capitalization stocks, which shows that this is a bullish market. Foreign investors are also showing more interest in medium-cap stocks," Nahum added.

"Trading was mixed, but the fact that the market did not decline despite some profit-taking is a very good sign. Investors are very optimistic and the trend is positive," said Amir Eayal of Epsilon Securities.
"I believe that even a decline in Wall Street stocks will not prevent the market from rising further," Eayal said.

The most active shares were Clal Israel, which lost 0.25 percent to 8,226 on volume of 5.2 million shekels; Bezeq Israel Telecom, which gained 0.5 percent to 789 on turnover of 4.6 million shekels, and Koor Industries, which closed unchanged at 28,008 on volume of 4.0 million shekels.
